verdict_reason: 10 of the 15 photos are on the sheet and they knit together into one site. Four are decisive: The Huc Bridge seen head-on with the Dac Nguyet Lau gate at its far end (2445608213); the Tran Ba Dinh pavilion, a square double-roofed pavilion on stone columns with incised couplets standing over the lake under a Vietnamese flag (2445610625); Hoan Kiem Lake with the red bridge across it (2445611463); and a bonsai on a stand at the lake edge in mist (2445610969). The interiors then chain onto those by shared fittings rather than by the geotag: the Van Xuong-style couplets '德流翰墨燦天章' and '位乘圖書闡泰運' with two tall gilded phoenixes (2445609449) sit in front of a red screen carrying gilt '壽' roundels, and the identical 壽-roundel screen and the identical cloud-handled stone censer reappear in 2338107718 and 2470435657 - so those three are the same building. 2446436750, 3505203250 and 3505208062 share the same bronze crane, the same white-plastered walls between red columns and the same green-and-red robed figures as each other. Nothing on the sheet contradicts a single temple complex, so this reads as a real place rather than a dump. Caveat: the ids form only about four blocks (2338..., 2445/2446..., 2470..., 3505...), and only the outdoor four are independently proven; the interior identification rests on within-batch and shared-fitting links.

photos.evidence: Upscaled 3x: red-lacquered temple front with open gilt-carved door leaves and a low tiled roof; inside, a red screen set with gilt openwork '壽' (longevity) roundels - the same screen as in 2445609449 - and in the foreground a stone censer with scrolled cloud-shaped handles, the same censer as in 2470435657. No name-board legible, so this is an identification by matching fittings to the frames that are proven.

Looking along the scarlet timber bridge deck with its red plank parapet and round red piles; at the far end stands the masonry gate-tower with the upswept roof and circular tympanum opening (Dac Nguyet Lau). Visitors walking towards the camera.

Upscaled 2.5x: shrine bay with two tall gilded phoenix statues, pairs of large famille-rose floor vases, a red altar and a red screen of gilt '壽' roundels. Whitewashed columns carry the couplet '德流翰墨燦天章' and '位乘圖書闡泰運' - 'brush and ink', 'charts and books' wording proper to Van Xuong De Quan, the literature deity enshrined at Ngoc Son. Notices read 'KHONG THAP HUONG, CAM HUONG TRONG DEN' and 'HOM CONG DUC'. Same photographer/batch as the confirmed Tran Ba Dinh and The Huc frames.

Upscaled 2.5x: a square two-tier pavilion with upswept tiled roofs on square stone columns bearing incised vertical inscriptions, open on all sides over grey lake water, a Vietnamese flag and a Buddhist flag on the ridge, potted bonsai and tourists on the flagstone terrace, and a small tower faintly visible out in the misty lake. This is the Tran Ba Dinh pavilion on the Ngoc Son island in Hoan Kiem Lake.

A bare-branched flowering bonsai in a dark pot on a low red timber stand at the very edge of a flagstone terrace, with grey misty lake water filling the rest of the frame - the same terrace edge, stone paving, pot furniture and weather as 2445610625, i.e. the Ngoc Son island.
Wide misty lake view: the low red arched timber bridge crossing to a tree-covered island at left with a red flag on it, still grey-green water, city trees beyond - Hoan Kiem Lake with The Huc Bridge.

Upscaled 2.5x: a red-and-gold altar under two gold ceremonial parasols with painted statues in a carved shrine frame, a large dark bronze crane standing on a tortoise at right, white-plastered walls between red columns, and a small gilt-on-red vertical plaque whose top character reads as '文' (a further zoom to 12x stayed too blurry to complete it, so I am not claiming to have read 'Van Xuong'). Same photographer-batch as the confirmed Tran Ba Dinh and bridge frames.

Upscaled 2.5x: red-lacquered temple facade with gilt-carved door panels standing open, incense smoke drifting, a large barrel drum and a small gilt-charactered plaque visible inside, and in the foreground the same stone censer with scrolled cloud-shaped handles seen in 2338107718 - i.e. the same front elevation as that frame, hence the same building as 2445609449.

Upscaled 2.5x: the same hall as 2446436750 - the identical dark bronze crane, the same green-robed and red-robed painted figures, the same white plaster wall behind red columns - now dressed with peach blossom and marigolds for Tet. A white-bearded scholar figure in a red gold-patterned robe stands at right.

Upscaled 5x on the board: a horizontal red name-board with faded gold characters, of which '九' and '天' and a third門-radical character are readable right-to-left, above a gilt openwork frieze; the crane, lacquer work and lighting match 3505203250 by the same photographer. The board itself was not fully readable, so the place rests on that within-batch match.
